title: The Signal That Matches the Decay Rate of a Dying Universe
hook: A repeating signal from deep space matches the theoretical decay signature of vacuum energy—what if the universe is dying and sending us a warning?
why_this_can_go_viral: Combines existential dread with a real unsolved mystery—viewers will share to ask 'could this be real?' and the horror of universal death is highly emotional.

title: The Asteroid That Passed Between Earth and the Moon—No One Saw It Coming
hook: A 100-meter asteroid slipped through Earth's orbital defense net, passing closer than many satellites—and our systems only caught it after it left.
why_this_can_go_viral: Taps into the primal fear of invisible danger and government failure—people love 'we almost died and didn't know' stories.

title: The Star That Exploded Twice—And Broke Everything We Know
hook: A supernova that should have been final reignited and exploded again, defying stellar death physics—and astronomers have no explanation.
why_this_can_go_viral: The idea of something dying and coming back to die again is deeply unsettling and counterintuitive, driving high curiosity.

title: The Dark Matter Cloud That Passed Through Earth 8 Years Ago
hook: A dense clump of dark matter may have drifted through our planet in 2016, disturbing atomic clocks—and we only noticed it afterward.
why_this_can_go_viral: The idea that an invisible, mass-altering entity passed through us without warning taps into sci-fi horror and real scientific mystery.

title: The Classified Space Telescope That Saw Something It Shouldn't
hook: A once-classified military telescope captured an object moving faster than light—and the image was immediately buried.
why_this_can_go_viral: Government secrets plus faster-than-light physics creates a perfect storm of conspiracy and awe—high shareability.

title: The Lost Continent That Existed Under Antarctica's Ice—And Then Vanished
hook: Radar scans revealed a landmass the size of Texas beneath Antarctic ice, but follow-up missions found nothing—it had disappeared.
why_this_can_go_viral: Combines Antarctic mystery with disappearance—two high-interest mystery triggers in one.

title: The Billion-Year-Old Signal That Arrived Last Tuesday
hook: A signal that traveled for a billion years hit our detectors last week—but its origin point is a region of space younger than Earth.
why_this_can_go_viral: Time paradoxes are viral gold—viewers will argue in comments about causality and feel the existential chill.

title: The Planet That Orbits Backward Through Its Own Solar System
hook: A gas giant is moving in retrograde—against the spin of its star—and it is slowly shredding its own solar system apart.
why_this_can_go_viral: Visual destruction and violation of cosmic order appeal to viewers who love 'the universe is broken' narratives.

title: The Neutrino That Hit Antarctica and Came from Beyond the Big Bang
hook: A ghost particle detected under the ice carried energy so high its origin may predate the universe—challenging the Big Bang itself.
why_this_can_go_viral: Challenges origin of everything—a deeply existential hook that invites debate and awe.

title: The Soviet Radar Station That Detected a Sky Full of Objects—Then Went Silent
hook: A remote Soviet radar array picked up thousands of objects entering the atmosphere simultaneously—then the station was decommissioned overnight.
why_this_can_go_viral: Cold War secrecy plus mass incursion creates immediate 'what did they see?' tension—high intrigue.

title: The Black Hole That Is Eating a Star—And It's on a Timer
hook: A black hole is consuming a star in a repeating pattern every 25 days—like a cosmic predator feeding on a schedule.
why_this_can_go_viral: Predator imagery is visceral and easy to visualize—feeds into fear of cosmic violence.

title: The Moon That Shouldn't Exist—And It's Pulling Its Planet Toward Us
hook: An impossibly large moon is orbiting a dead planet, and its gravity is dragging that world into an intercept course with Earth.
why_this_can_go_viral: Adds a specific countdown tension and 'impossible' science—viewers will speculate on impact.

title: The Data That Disappeared from Every Voyager Probe at the Same Time
hook: Both Voyager probes stopped transmitting certain data streams simultaneously—as if something turned off a switch across the solar system.
why_this_can_go_viral: Symmetry and simultaneity imply deliberate action—viewers will jump to alien or hidden-system theories.

title: The Star That Has a Constant, Unexplainable 'Bump' in Its Light Curve
hook: A star in the Milky Way displays a perfect, repeating dip—like a sphere orbiting—but no visible object is there.
why_this_can_go_viral: Tabby's Star is already famous—this renews mystery with 'still no explanation' angle.

title: The Dark Matter Experiment That Detected Something—Then Never Spoke Again
hook: An underground dark matter detector registered a single anomalous event—and the team that published it immediately went silent.
why_this_can_go_viral: Silence implies suppression—viewers will speculate on what was 'too dangerous' to share.

title: The Comet That Will Hit Earth—But Not in the Way You Think
hook: A long-period comet is on course to impact the moon, sending a debris wave straight toward Earth's surface.
why_this_can_go_viral: Unexpected secondary impact mechanism is novel—viewers will be surprised by 'moon bounce' disaster.

title: The Fossil That Proves an Asteroid Didn't Kill the Dinosaurs—Something Else Did
hook: A fossil found deep in the K-Pg boundary layer shows life existed for 30,000 years after the impact—something else finished them off.
why_this_can_go_viral: Challenges a widely taught narrative—viewers love 'everything you know is wrong' content.

title: The Galaxy That Has No Dark Matter—And That's More Terrifying Than Having It
hook: A galaxy with zero dark matter means gravity works differently there—and it could mean our universe is a simulation.
why_this_can_go_viral: Taps into simulation hypothesis—a highly viral concept that sparks endless debate.

title: The NASA Budget Item That Paid for a 'Deep Space Weapon'—And Was Hidden
hook: A single line in NASA's budget read 'Deep Space Countermeasure System'—and the program was classified the next day.
why_this_can_go_viral: Budget line reveals a secret—creates immediate 'what are they hiding' tension with military implications.

title: The Great Silence That Lasted 2 Billion Years—And Then Life Exploded
hook: Earth was a silent, barren rock for two billion years—then suddenly, the entire planet erupted in complex life. Why?
why_this_can_go_viral: The gap implies an external trigger—viewers will speculate on 'who or what hit the switch.'

title: The Signal That Matches a Dead Language—And No One Sent It
hook: A radio burst from a dead star encodes a pattern identical to an ancient Earth language that has no known speakers.
why_this_can_go_viral: Connects human ancient mystery with alien signal—a double hook that appeals to history and space fans.

title: The Planet Where It Rains Glass Sideways—And It Never Stops
hook: Winds of 5,000 mph carry shards of molten glass horizontally across a planet that is tidally locked to a dying star.
why_this_can_go_viral: Visceral, easy-to-imagine horror—'hell planet' narratives are highly shareable.

title: The Declassified Memo That Describes an Alien 'Quarantine' of Earth
hook: A declassified CIA memo from 1971 suggests extraterrestrial intelligences have placed Earth under observation—and we can't leave.
why_this_can_go_viral: Government document + quarantine narrative = immediate 'are we prisoners?' reaction—high conspiracy shareability.

title: The Empty Region That Is Wait—Something Is There Now
hook: A void in space that was empty for decades now has a faint object—something appeared from nothing.
why_this_can_go_viral: 'Something from nothing' is a fundamental violation—creates intense curiosity and debate.

title: The Gamma Ray Burst That Is Aimed Exactly at Earth—And We Don't Know When
hook: A nearby star system is showing pre-supernova signs, and its magnetic axis points directly at Earth—a future extinction event.
why_this_can_go_viral: Inescapable, invisible, and timed—a perfect recipe for existential panic and high engagement.
